Justyna Gudzowska: Justyna Gudzowska has spent her career at the intersection of illicit finance and international security.  She is an expert on sanctions, corruption, terrorism financing, and money laundering, having worked on these issues across the public and private sectors. She is currently the Executive Director of The Sentry, an investigative and policy organization that seeks to expose and disrupt actors profiting from the conflict, corruption, and natural resource exploitation that drive human suffering. She is also an Adjunct Professor at Georgetown University's School of Foreign Service (SFS) where she teaches a class on illicit finance, and an Associate Fellow at the UK-based Royal United Services Institute (RUSI). She has taught at Yale Law School as a Visiting Lecturer in Law. Prior to joining The Sentry, Justyna was the lead sanctions attorney at Morgan Stanley, a counter-terrorism financing expert at the UN Security Council, and a sanctions attorney at the US Department of the Treasury.

Katie Ellena is co-founder of Partnerships for Integrity (P4I), a democracy and governance non-profit based in Germany and operating around the globe, and CEO of The Concord Project, a U.S. democracy non-profit. She is a non-profit executive and lawyer with 20+ years of experience partnering with election commissions, oversight bodies, anti-corruption commissions, tribunals, courts, and civil society in over 30 countries. Katja Bechtel:
Workshop Coordinator for SMEs at the Sharp End: Integrity Risks, Power Asymmetries, and Practical Solutions (8.6)

Katja is an international expert in business integrity, anti-corruption, and governance with over 15 years of global leadership experience at the World Economic Forum and Transparency International. She has advised organizations including UNITAR, ISO, and USAID on anti-corruption, financial crime, and public-private collaboration, and has designed and led high-impact multi-stakeholder initiatives. She has held leadership roles within the Business 20 (B20), the official business engagement group of the G20. A seasoned speaker and recognized thought leader, Katja works at the intersection of business, policy, and civil society to advance integrity as a strategic leadership imperative.
Ketakandriana Rafitoson: Ketakandriana “Ke” Rafitoson is a Political scientist and a Human Rights Defender from Madagascar. Ke holds a PhD in Political science from IEP Madagascar and a PhD in Social sciences applied to Development from the Catholic University of Madagascar, where she is also lecturing. She is a member of the International Board of the Fisheries Transparency Initiative (FiTI), and of the African Women Against Corruption Network (AWACN)’s Advisory Board, and is also serving as the volunteer National Coordinator of the Publish What You Pay (PWYP) Coalition in Madagascar.

Klaus Moosmayer:
Klaus Moosmayer was elected on May 22 2025 as member of the Supervisory Board of Deutsche Bank AG and serves on the Audit, Risk and Compensation Control Committees of the Board. Prior this appointment Klaus was until April 2025 the Chief Ethics, Risk and Compliance Officer and member of the Executive Committee of Novartis, a position he took over in December 2018. At Novartis, after closing out the legacy compliance matters of the corporation, he brought together ethics, policy governance, risk&crisis management and internal controls to an integrated assurance system which also included the responsible use of AI and new technologies. As a member of the Executive Committee he reported to the CEO and interacted closely with the Board of Directors including the Risk and Audit&Compliance Committee.

Before joining Novartis, Klaus spent 18 years in management positions of increasing responsibility at Siemens AG, serving as the company’s Chief Compliance Officer the last five years. Since 2006, he has been member of the core team tasked with addressing and resolving Siemens’ global corruption crisis.

He began his career after studying law and obtaining his doctor of jurisprudence at the university of Freiburg as an attorney and criminal defense lawyer.

Klaus Moosmayer has held Board and leadership positions at various international institutions. He led over many years the Anticorruption Committee of Business at OECD and subsequently served on its Executive Board. He was also Chair or Co-Chair of the B20 Integrity task forces during the G20 presidencies of Germany, Argentina, Saudi-Arabia, Indonesia and Italy. From 2021 until 2025 Klaus was Board member of SwissHoldings, the business association of Swiss based multinational companies.
Klaus publishes extensively in German, English and Spanish on ethics, risk management, compliance and governance and speaks frequently on these topics at national and international conferences. He was the first Chief Compliance Officer to speak in front of the General Assembly of the United Nations. In 2023, he was appointed to serve on the Council of the International Anti-Corruption Conference, which in collaboration with the government of the host country and the Secretariat of Transparency International organizes by-annually the world’s largest international gathering on integrity. In early 2025 he was appointed co-chair of the Global Future Council on Good Governance of the World Economic Forum for the term 2025-2026.

Kristen is a graduate of the Washington College of Law at American University in Washington, DC, where she specialized in international law, earning a Juris Doctorate with honors.

Kristin Jean Rosella: Kristin Rosella is the Executive Director of LexCollective, a global coalition of lawyers and investigators working on interconnected human rights issues. She has trained over 1,000 civil society members, prosecutors, and law enforcement across Southeast Asia, East Africa, Latin America, and Eurasia.

Kumi Naidoo:
Kumi Naidoo is a human rights and climate justice activist from South Africa. He was Executive Director of Greenpeace International (from 2009 through 2015) and Secretary General of Amnesty International (from 2018 through 2019). Naidoo also served as the Secretary-General of CIVICUS, the international alliance for citizen participation, from 1998 to 2008.

He was an activist against the apartheid regime and its educational system in South Africa. Naidoo’s activism went from neighborhood organizing and community youth work to civil disobedience with mass mobilisations against the white controlled apartheid government. He has written about his activism in this period in his memoirs titled, “Letters to My Mother: The Making of a Troublemaker.

Laura Ferris is an attorney and former US federal prosecutor for the United States Department of Justice. She is an expert on sanctions, terrorism financing, transnational criminal organizations, environmental crimes, and money laundering.

During her time as a prosecutor, Laura specialized on fraud, money laundering, violent crimes, and terrorism, serving three years as the Chief of the White-Collar Crime Unit. Laura led and worked with several criminal task forces, including the Joint Terrorism Task Force (JTTF), as well as Hi-tech Crimes and SARs (Suspicious Activity Reports) Review task forces.

From 2015-2022, Laura served with the US. Department of the Treasury as legal advisor to the Office of Foreign Assets Control on several sanctions programs and then as Assistant Chief Counsel, Enforcement and Liaison Divisions, for the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), the US financial intelligence unit.  At FinCEN she also served as Chief of Staff and Special Advisor to the Director.  In 2019 she established an overseas FinCEN position based out of the US Embassy in The Netherlands working at Europol as a liaison officer focused on increasing sharing of financial intelligence related to transnational criminal and national security threats. While overseas she also developed and led FinCEN’s first environmental crimes initiative, including outreach, information sharing, partnership meetings, and FinCEN’s first environmental crime publications, specifically an Environmental Crime Notice and a Financial Threat Analysis on Illegal Wildlife Trafficking.

Currently, Laura serves as the Director of Programs for the Sentry.

Linas Pernavas:
Mr Linas Pernavas from the 19th of June, 2023 is serving as a Director of the Special Investigation Service of the Republic of Lithuania.

In 1999 he graduated from the Lithuanian University of Law, in 2005 from Vilnius University and obtained a Master of Law qualification.

With a career spanning over two decades, Mr Pernavas joined the interior affairs system in 1995 and steadily climbed the ranks. His career began at the Ignalina District Police Headquarters.

In 2005-2008 he was the Chief of Zarasai District Police Headquarters, in 2008-2014 he served as a Chief of Utena County Police Headquarters and in 2014 he was a Chief of Kaunas District Police Headquarters.

Between 2014 and 2019 he was the Commissioner General of Lithuanian Police.

Mr. Pernavas launched the Police reform which increased public safety, increased the number of police officers on patrol and improved working conditions for officers. The reform made it possible to double the number of officers on the streets, to respond more quickly to the most dangerous calls, and to raise officers’ salaries. During his service as the Commissioner General of Lithuanian Police the public trust in police was on the rise and the highest.

Mr. Pernavas together with other heads of the Lithuanian Police established the Charity and Support Fund for Police Employees. The main and only purpose of the fund is to help officials and employees in extremely critical and difficult situations.

From 2019 (November) till 2023 (June) he served as Lithuania’s police attaché to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and remained there.

In May 2023 the Lithuanian Parliament approved Mr Pernavas as the director of the Special Investigation Service of the Republic of Lithuania. The agency’s main functions are the investigation of corruption cases, corruption prevention, and anti-corruption intelligence.

In 2023 he was elected as the President of the European Partners Against Corruption (EPAC) and the European Union Anti-Corruption Contact Network (EACN). EPAC/EACN is the largest and oldest European network of anti-corruption authorities and police oversight bodies. The aim of the EPAC/EACN network is to strengthen cooperation in the exchange of good practice in the fight against corruption and police oversight.

Mr Pernavas was awarded numerous times throughout his career: the Officer’s Cross of the Order of the Grand Duke Gediminasof Lithuania, the Medal of the Lithuanian Armed Forces “For Merit”, the 1st Degree Cross “100 for Estonian Police”, the 1st Degree Badge of Honour of the Dignitary Protection Service and many other.

Maiwand Rahyab:
Maiwand Rahyab is the founder and C.E.O. of Resilient Societies, an emerging global initiative dedicated to protecting civic space and empowering democracy advocates and human rights defenders working under authoritarian regimes or in exile. Resilient Societies advances inclusive platforms such as the Resilience Network and the Ottawa Civic Space Summit, helping restore the voice, agency and relevance of civil society actors confronting repression and transnational threats.

She has directed Cívitas Venezuela since 2005. In 2016 she founded and directed Vendata. In 2006 she co-founded Crea Resultados. In 2017 she launched and led CampusTransparencia.com, an online training platform on transparency, justice, integrity, and anti-corruption; and in 2019, Espaja.com, a news and discourse verification platform, and the national Anti-Corruption Coalition movement. She co-founded and directed Becrack in 2020. She is a member of the coordinating team of Quiero Elegir.

Since 2020 she has served on the board of the Venezuela Corruption Taskforce. Since 2023 she has been a member of the Board of Directors of the Latin American and Caribbean Network for Democracy (REDLAD). She was invited as a civil-society speaker to the United Nations Security Council in special sessions on Venezuela in September 2018 and January 2026.

Since 2000 she has been a Fellow of Ashoka, the global network of social entrepreneurs, and in 2006 she won Ashoka's Champion ChangeMakers award. In 2019 she received the Anti-Corruption Leader Annual Award from the Americas Society/Council of the Americas. She was a member of ChangeMakers United in 2021. In 2024 she received Transparency International's Amalia Award for Individual Professional Excellence.

She has led more than 70 investigations into corruption networks, money laundering, and organized crime in Venezuela; has designed and directed dozens of events; and has been invited as a speaker and panelist at dozens of international events across dozens of countries.
Micol Martini:
Workshop Coordinator for Nature, Money, Conflict: How to Disrupt the Financial Drivers of Environmental Crime and Insecurity (1.4)

Micol Martini is a Senior Expert with over 20 years of experience working on issues related to governance, conflict, and insecurity.
Mitzi Jonelle Tan: Mitzi Jonelle Tan is a full-time climate justice activist based in Metro Manila, Philippines. She is an organizer with Fridays For Future International and FFF MAPA (Most Affected Peoples and Areas) making sure that voices from the Global South are heard, amplified, and given space. She is also part of the steering committee of the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty and the Youth Climate Justice Fund. A strong voice on anti-imperialism, anti-colonization, and the intersectionality of the climate crisis, she is committed to changing the system and building a world that prioritizes people and planet, not profit, through collective action, system change, love and joy.
Mohammed Benalilou: President, L'Instance nationale de la probité, de la prévention et de la lutte contre la corruption (INPPLC)
Moritz Homann: Moritz Homann is Head of AI at EQS Group, a global software provider for Compliance & Ethics solutions. He leads the company’s AI transformation across both product innovation and internal adoption, with a strong focus on trusted AI, auditability, and governance. His work centers on how organizations can use AI responsibly in high-trust and regulated environments while creating practical value at scale. Moritz is a regular speaker at conferences, webinars, and industry events, and he led EQS Group’s AI Model Benchmark project, testing how leading AI models perform on Compliance & Ethics tasks.
Naomi Roht-Arriaza: Co-Chair of the Victims of Corruption Working Group of the Global Civil Society Coalition for the UNCAC and author of Fighting Grand Corruption: Transnational and Human Rights Approaches in Latin America and Beyond
Nicola Allocca:
Nicola Allocca is an international executive, lecturer, and thought leader in governance, risk management, compliance, and anti-corruption, with a strong focus on the integration of artificial intelligence into business decision-making.

He currently serves as Chair of the Business at OECD (BIAC) Integrity & Anti-Corruption Committee, where he leads global initiatives to promote transparency, ethical business conduct, and resilient governance systems. He has also played a key role in international policy dialogues, including the B20, contributing to the advancement of integrity frameworks in complex and rapidly evolving environments.

With cross-industry experience spanning infrastructure, aerospace, steel, consulting, and retail, Nicola has held senior leadership roles where he has driven the transformation of compliance from a control function into a strategic enabler of performance and value creation.

He also serves as a Short-Term Expert for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI), contributing to international capacity-building projects focused on governance, legality, and institutional strengthening.

Alongside his executive career, he teaches Responsible Business Conduct at the University of Rome Tor Vergata and contributes to international master programs focused on public procurement and anti-corruption.

His work sits at the intersection of governance and innovation, advocating for a model where there is no trade-off between performance and compliance, and where AI is recognized as a new stakeholder in organizational ecosystem
Nicolás Crow:
Workshop Coordinator for Integrity First: How Gen Z Is Reframing Anti-Corruption to Unlock the SDGs (11.7)

Nicolas Crow is an Ecuadorian lawyer, Ambassador of the International Organization of Youth, and Founder and Executive Director of the YAC Foundation, one of the largest youth-led anti-corruption organizations in the Americas. The foundation focuses on governance, transparency, and combating public corruption to advance sustainable development. Having grown up in Ecuador and witnessed the country’s transformation from being considered one of the safest nations in Latin America to facing an unprecedented security crisis, Nicolas developed a strong interest in understanding how public corruption and institutional weaknesses directly impact people’s lives, opportunities, and development prospects, particularly for young people.

Alongside his work at the YAC Foundation, Nicolas operates at the intersection of international law, public policy, public and regulatory affairs, and emerging technologies. He is committed to fostering collaboration among stakeholders to address emerging challenges and deliver tangible development outcomes, while advocating for stronger anti-corruption efforts and greater youth participation in national and international decision-making processes. Nicolas holds a law degree from Universidad San Francisco de Quito and has pursued further studies at the University of Cambridge, Peking University, and Beijing International Studies University, including coursework in development economics and Mandarin Chinese.
Nina Chanturia:
Workshop Coordinator and Rapporteur for Integrity or Illusion? Strengthening Anti-Corruption to Safeguard Democracy (3.1)

Workshop Coordinator for Igniting Integrity in Public Decision-Making (9.1)

Nina Chanturia is an Associate Democratic Governance Officer at the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) and its Anti-Corruption Focal Point. She works with parliaments, political parties, and anti-corruption bodies to strengthen oversight, integrity systems, lobbying regulation, and transparency in political finance.

With over a decade of experience in democratization and EU integration, she has supported OSCE/ODIHR Election Observation Missions since 2013. She also served at the Embassy of Georgia to the Netherlands, chaired the Women’s Democracy Network in Georgia under the International Republican Institute, and managed leadership programs funded by the United Nations Democracy Fund.

Nina holds a Master of Public Policy from the Willy Brandt School of Public Policy and is a PhD candidate researching the EU’s impact on association countries.
Nina Jankowicz: Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, American Sunlight Project.
